format.chart: 32-team double-elimination bracket with reseeding at every stage (Joe, 2026-10-23). Winners bracket stages of 16/8/4/2/1 series counting the opening round; losers bracket stages of 8/8/4/4/2/2/1/1, alternating survivor-only and drop-in rounds; grand final plus one reset series if the one-loss finalist wins the first final. 62 series total, 63 with the reset. At every stage the pool is reseeded by original tournament seed and paired highest vs lowest, second-highest vs second-lowest, so the top seed always draws the lowest-seeded survivor. See BRACKET.md.
format.home_pattern: 2-2-1-1-1, higher seed home first (Joe, 2026-10-23): Games 1-2 higher seed, 3-4 lower seed, 5 higher seed, 6 lower seed, 7 higher seed.
format.formation_gate: A stage forms only when every series feeding it is complete: Winners Round 2 and Losers Round 1 form when all 16 opening series finish; each later stage forms when its feeding stage finishes (plus the corresponding winners stage for losers drop-in stages). No pairing exists before its stage forms (Joe's reseeding rule, 2026-10-23).
format.final: Winners-bracket champion (undefeated) vs losers-bracket champion (one loss), best of 7; if the one-loss team wins, one reset series decides the championship.

stat_keying: Player stats are stored per (team, player_id). A player rostered by two teams has one line per team, never merged.

series.label: Opening Round, Series 2
series.provenance: Played in Payoff Pitch as a standalone governed series on 2026-10-24 (FAC deck mode, version 2 pitcher cards, the pitcher addendum, manager traits, the fatigue fix layer from Game 3) and adopted into the tournament as R1-02 by Joe's ruling, the same adoption as R1-01. Box data is built from the series' saved state files (payoff-pitch-nationals/state_series_sf_wsh_g1..g5.json) by record_r1_02_pp_adoption.py. Field mapping: rolls holds the FAC flip history (card number and draw purpose), the Payoff Pitch equivalent of the dice record; final_grades is empty because Payoff Pitch has no letter grades, and pitcher fatigue end states are in fatigue_end_states; resolutions and n41 are null because those APBA counters do not exist in Payoff Pitch; batting sac is the states' single SH category, with sf and ibb null because the states do not split them; pitching lines carry hr allowed, which the states record, and hb null, which they do not record by pitcher.

carry.arms: Bullpen availability resets between rounds; no pitcher carries a restriction out of this series. Availability inside the series ran under the house outs convention and no reliever was ever capped.

series.label: Opening Round, Series 3
series.provenance: Played in Payoff Pitch as tournament series R1-03 on 2026-10-24 (FAC deck mode, version 2 pitcher cards, the pitcher addendum, manager traits for both clubs: Francona for Boston, Cash for Tampa Bay in tournament mode with the Opener refused under Joe's ruling that relievers do not start tournament games; the fatigue fix layer in both games) under Joe's ruling that the tournament is a Payoff Pitch tournament and APBA is closed. Games 1-2 are recorded here from the series' saved state files (payoff-pitch-rays/state_series_bos_tb_g1..g2.json) by record_r1_03_pp.py, following the R1-02 script's mechanism; the series is in progress, Boston leading 2-0, and later games append the same way. Tampa Bay plays in the host engine's 'PHA' guest slot, so the state files key the Rays as 'PHA'; those keys map to TB in the records. Field mapping: rolls holds the FAC flip history (card number and draw purpose), the Payoff Pitch equivalent of the dice record; final_grades is empty because Payoff Pitch has no letter grades, and pitcher fatigue end states are in fatigue_end_states, from the fix layer stored in both states; resolutions and n41 are null because those APBA counters do not exist in Payoff Pitch; batting sac is the states' single SH category, with sf and ibb null because the states do not split them; pitching lines carry hr allowed, which the states record, and hb null, which they do not record by pitcher. Availability ran under the house outs convention: caps_in and caps_out carry it in the archive's encoding (player_id: max outs next game, 0 would mean unavailable). Games 3-7 were added from Joe's official box scores on 2026-10-25. Those box scores carry the linescore, batting, pitching, decisions, and the short recap. They do not carry the FAC roll log, so games/R1-03-G3.json through G7.json store an empty rolls array. Games 3-7 have no per-game calendar date in the box scores; the date is null. The series summary dates the series to 2026-10-24 and 2026-10-25. Games 1-2 stay dated 2026-10-24. Boston won the series 4-3 and advances on the winners side at 1-0. Tampa Bay drops to the losers side at 0-1 and is not eliminated.

carry.rotation_note: Series complete, Boston 4-3. Starters in the box scores: Boston Martinez, Clemens, Young, Wood, Grove, Martinez, Clemens; Tampa Bay Price, Shields, Snell, McClanahan, Kazmir, Price, Shields.

narratives.text: In Game 1, Pedro Martinez threw a no-hitter, nine innings, no hits, two walks, eleven strikeouts, and Jimmie Foxx homered twice in a 6-0 win.

In Game 2, Roger Clemens struck out fourteen over 7.1 innings; Toby Hall's sixth-inning homer gave Tampa Bay its first lead of the series, and Boston answered with three runs in the bottom of the inning against a fatigued James Shields, Jonathan Papelbon closing the 3-1 win.

In Game 3, Blake Snell threw a complete-game shutout, three hits and eight strikeouts, and the only run scored in the bottom of the ninth: Carl Crawford doubled off Cy Young and Joey Wendle doubled him home off Papelbon.

In Game 4, all six Tampa Bay runs were charged to Smoky Joe Wood, on Jason Bartlett's three-run homer in the fourth and Carlos Pena's three-run homer in the seventh; Shane McClanahan won 6-3 at 8.2 innings, and Foxx homered twice in the loss.

Game 5 was the turn of the series. Tampa Bay led 5-0 into the seventh at Fenway. Nomar Garciaparra's homer got Boston started, and the ninth produced four runs: Scott Kazmir left with a three-run lead, no outs and runners on first and third, both inherited runners scored, and Ted Williams tied the game with a single off Pete Fairbanks. Papelbon, in since the eighth, held Tampa Bay through the tenth while fatigued, and Foxx led off the bottom of the tenth with the walk-off homer, 6-5.

Tampa Bay leveled it a second time in Game 6, and did it against Martinez at his best: he threw a complete game, four hits and eleven strikeouts, and lost 3-1 because every run in the game scored in the third inning. Boston's run came home on a double play; Bartlett tripled, Hall singled him in, and Wendle hit a two-run homer. David Price walked nobody in eight innings and Fairbanks saved it.

Game 7 belonged to Clemens. He went 8.2 innings, five hits, one earned run, one walk, sixteen strikeouts, and was never fatigued. Tampa Bay's only run was Evan Longoria's fourth-inning homer. Shields broke in the fifth, when two Boston runs scored on bases-loaded walks against his fatigued reads, and Boston ran the score to 8-1. Papelbon recorded the final out.

series.label: Opening Round, Series 4
series.provenance: Played in Payoff Pitch as tournament series R1-04 on 2026-10-25 (FAC deck mode, version 2 pitcher cards, the pitcher addendum, the fatigue fix layer, and manager traits governing both clubs: Sparky Anderson for Detroit, Bob Brenly for Arizona, with the official bunt-grade overlay live for Brenly's Small Ball) under Joe's ruling that the tournament is a Payoff Pitch tournament and APBA is closed. Detroit home games (1, 2, 5) were played on the 1986 Tiger Stadium park card under Joe's ruling; Arizona home games (3, 4, 6) on the standard league-average composite park Joe accepted; the printed Chase Field card from the publisher's 2024 set was verified into the managers' reference folder but never adopted. The series is recorded here from the series' saved state files (payoff-pitch-diamondbacks/state_series_det_ari_g1..g6.json) by record_r1_04_pp.py, following the R1-03 scripts' mechanism, and it is COMPLETE: Detroit wins 4-2. Game 5 was played twice on 2026-10-25: the first playing (Arizona 8, Detroit 5, seed 20261212) was set aside by Joe's ruling after he had the game played fresh from scratch, and the fresh re-play (Detroit 3, Arizona 1, seed 20261220) stands as the official Game 5 recorded here; the superseded playing is preserved in the series home (PP_R1_04_G5_SUPERSEDED.md and its state files) and recorded nowhere in this archive. Detroit played Games 3-6 under Joe's lineup ruling: Harry Heilmann started in left field in Bobby Veach's batting slot, priced straight across on his carded right-field line, and Veach never appeared in the series after Game 2. Game 1 was stopped in the first inning at an unanswerable rare-play branch and resumed under Joe's count-based carry ruling (the lingering-effects wrapper extended with count-based TOUGH and IN-PLAY flags). Arizona plays in the host engine's 'OPP' guest slot, so the state files key the Diamondbacks as 'OPP'; those keys map to ARI in the records. Field mapping: rolls holds the FAC flip history (card number and draw purpose), the Payoff Pitch equivalent of the dice record; final_grades is empty because Payoff Pitch has no letter grades, and pitcher fatigue end states are in fatigue_end_states, from the fix layer stored in every state, except the two 0-BF phantom changes (Andrew Chafin in Game 2, Dizzy Trout in Game 4, each a driver-recorded change after the final out, disclosed in those game records), who faced no batter, carry no fatigue record in their states, and are recorded unfatigued; resolutions and n41 are null because those APBA counters do not exist in Payoff Pitch; batting sac is the states' single SH category, with sf and ibb null because the states do not split them; pitching lines carry hr allowed, which the states record, and hb null, which they do not record by pitcher. Availability ran under the house outs convention: caps_in and caps_out carry it in the archive's encoding (player_id: max outs next game, 0 means unavailable). Detroit advances on the winners side at 1-0 in series; Arizona drops to the losers side at 0-1 and is not eliminated. No later-round shell fills from this series alone: Winners Round 2 and Losers Round 1 form only when all 16 opening series are complete (the formation gate), and advance_bracket was run at completion and changed nothing outside this series.

carry.rotation_note: Series complete, Detroit 4-2. Starters in the box scores: Detroit Newhouser, Verlander, Lolich, Bridges, Morris, Newhouser; Arizona Johnson, Schilling, Webb, Gallen, Kelly, Johnson.

narratives.text: In Game 1, Randy Johnson threw eight scoreless innings of four-hit ball at Tiger Stadium; Arizona's runs came on singles off Hal Newhouser in the fourth and fifth, and the closer rule lifted Johnson at 24 outs with the two-run lead, Jose Valverde finishing the 2-0 shutout.

In Game 2, Arizona won 7-5 in thirteen innings. Detroit's three-run sixth, on Hank Greenberg's two-run triple, took a 4-3 lead; Corbin Carroll tied it with a seventh-inning homer, Gabriel Moreno's tenth-inning squeeze put Arizona ahead, Charlie Gehringer answered with a leadoff homer, and Ketel Marte's two-run homer in the thirteenth won it, Byung-Hyun Kim getting George Kell with the bases loaded for the save after Valverde was ejected for hitting Bill Freehan a second time.

In Game 3, Detroit's first inning decided it: Ty Cobb singled and stole second, Gehringer tripled him home and Al Kaline singled in a second run, and Mickey Lolich allowed three hits in seven innings in a 4-1 win. Harry Heilmann, starting in left field under Joe's lineup ruling, doubled and scored in the seventh. Freehan was ejected in the first inning, before he batted, for arguing a rare-play call.

In Game 4, Tommy Bridges threw a three-hitter with thirteen strikeouts and no Arizona runner reached third; Zac Gallen pitched a complete game and lost 3-0 on two earned runs. Willie Hernandez, capped at three outs by the rest rule, had to be lifted in the ninth in a save situation, and Denny McLain recorded the save.

Game 5 was played twice, and only the second playing counts. Jack Morris was scoreless into the eighth and Merrill Kelly threw a complete-game one-hitter and lost: George Kell's two-run triple was Detroit's only hit, and the third run scored hitless in the seventh on two Arizona errors and a squeeze. Hernandez saved the 3-1 win. The first playing, an 8-5 Arizona win, was set aside by Joe's ruling and is not in this archive.

Game 6 ended the series in Arizona. Detroit scored five runs with two out in the third off Johnson, Heilmann's three-run homer the decisive swing, and a sixth run in the fourth ended Johnson's night on the six-run fatigue line. Newhouser won 10-3, and Hernandez pitched the last three innings scoreless for the save, escaping a bases-loaded, no-out jam in the seventh.

series.label: Opening Round, Series 5
series.provenance: Played in Payoff Pitch as tournament series R1-05 on 2026-10-26 (FAC deck mode, version 2 pitcher cards, the pitcher addendum live for both clubs, the fatigue fix layer, the official bunt-grade overlay at the bunt seam, the universal DH, manager traits for both clubs: La Russa for St. Louis, Black for Colorado) under Joe's ruling that the tournament is a Payoff Pitch tournament and APBA is closed. Game 1 is recorded here from the series' saved state file (payoff-pitch-rockies/state_series_stl_col_g1.json) by record_r1_05_g1_pp.py, following the R1-03 scripts' mechanism; the series is in progress, St. Louis leading 1-0, and later games append the same way. Colorado plays in the host engine's 'OPP' guest slot, so the state file keys the Rockies as 'OPP'; those keys map to COL in the records. Field mapping: rolls holds the FAC flip history (card number and draw purpose), the Payoff Pitch equivalent of the dice record; final_grades is empty because Payoff Pitch has no letter grades, and pitcher fatigue end states are in fatigue_end_states, from the fix layer stored in the state; resolutions and n41 are null because those APBA counters do not exist in Payoff Pitch; batting sac is the state's single SH category, with sf and ibb null because the states do not split them; pitching lines carry hr allowed, which the states record, and hb null, which they do not record by pitcher. Game 1 contained two hand-resolved rare plays: Ozzie Smith was ejected after striking out on the Bases Empty TOUGH 06-12 entry in the bottom of the 1st (Ted Simmons replaced him at shortstop under the engine's substitution fallback), and a Bases Empty TOUGH 90-99 foul tip off catcher Elias Diaz in the bottom of the 4th resolved under the not-injured branch because the converted cards carry no position-player injury ratings; its remains-in clause governed the inning's last two plate appearances. Ryan Helsley finished the 9th with no save: he entered with one out, the bases empty and a three-run lead, so the tying run was neither on base, at bat nor on deck at his entry and his two outs are short of the one-inning prong. Availability ran under the house outs convention: caps_in and caps_out carry it in the archive's encoding (player_id: max outs next game, 0 meaning unavailable).

carry.rotation_note: Each club opened with its first starter in posted order (STL: Bob Gibson; COL: Ubaldo Jimenez). Game 2 is at St. Louis: Dizzy Dean vs Kyle Freeland. Full posted orders: STL Gibson, Dean, Wainwright, Brecheen, Carpenter; COL Jimenez, Freeland, Cook, Marquez, Chacin.
carry.arms: Availability inside the series runs under the house outs convention. Jason Isringhausen recorded 9 outs in Game 1 and is unavailable for Game 2. No other pitcher is capped going into Game 2: the remaining Game 1 relief outs were Logan 5, Street 4, Betancourt 2, Helsley 2. The starters' next turns run on the posted rotation. Bullpen availability resets between rounds.

games.game_recap: The New York Yankees beat the Miami Marlins 6-2. The go-ahead run scored in the 7th inning. Derek Jeter led the New York Yankees offense with 2 hits and 1 RBI in 3 at-bats. Whitey Ford earned the win, allowing 2 earned runs in 7.2 innings.
